items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1976-02-19
items.q: Daviesi's Gollywag Cakewalk, for example, contains precisely those elements before the Modern Jazz Quartet existed.

ctx.x: Okay, but how do you fit in the fact that, for instance, they have, uh... Oh, uh... One of the players plays a bass, and there's a beat that's, uh... That's a rhythmic beat that is, uh... identified with jazz or with Afro-American...

Uh... I'm contending that that actually does not occur. Uh-huh. And that all of those elements which you are mentioning already do exist in these other composers. Uh-huh. Uh... Daviesi's Gollywag Cakewalk, for example, contains precisely those elements before the Modern Jazz Quartet
existed. In other words, there's nothing Afro-American about the Modern Jazz Quartet.
